newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian automaker GAZ plans new models.
newsitem.headline: Russian automaker GAZ plans new models.

text.p: AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod (GAZ), Russia's second-largest automaker, said on Tuesday it planned to build several new cars and trucks in 1997 but gave no details on costs and financing of the new models.
"Since 1994, we have been diversifying our product range to meet the changing needs of our customers," GAZ President Nikolai Pugin told an automotive conference in Moscow.
By mid-1997, GAZ plans to start manufacturing new cars, pickups, sports-utility vehicles and trucks of various weights, Pugin said.
It also expects to offer new modifications of its vehicles for the construction industry, the military and public safety services.
Pugin displayed photographs and sketches of the new models at the conference, but the future of the vehicles is uncertain.
Since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, Russian automakers have presented with fanfare many designs and prototypes of future products.
However they never entered serial production, mainly because the plans have hinged on foreign investment, which has been negligible in Russia compared to other countries in former communist Europe.

"Russia has received very little of the investment dollars that are currently flowing into emerging markets, (but) we believe this should and will change," Dagmar Bottenbruch, research director at MC Securities in London, said in a speech made available to Reuters that she was due to deliver at the conference on Wednesday.

However, analysts said, GAZ's plans have some credence as the automaker had showed it could deliver on its promises in the early 1990s to produce a light-commercial vehicle, named Gazelle, which now is the most popular truck sold in Russia.

One new model, Sobol, is a 2.8-tonne truck based on the 3.5-tonne version of the Gazelle, Pugin said. The Sobol also will include features to improve riding comfort and performance, such as independent suspensions and power steering, he said.
GAZ also plans four-wheel-drive versions of Sobel as pickups and sporty utility vehicles, he added.
Pugin said GAZ is road-testing another commercial vehicle to be ready for production by May 1997 -- four-wheel-drive military trucks with payloads of two tonnes to four tonnes.
In addition to trucks, GAZ plans to introduce a second car, a still-unnamed mid-sized model, to complement its core product, the Volga sedan, Pugin said.
"We have designed a completely new car, and we will be ready at the end of this year to enlist a world-class engineering firm to help us," he said.

The Russian automaker also plans to diversify the rear-wheel-drive Volga to offer versions with four-wheel drive and front-wheel drive, Pugin said. By March 1997, all Volgas will feature new breaks, chassis, power steering, seats, tyres and wheels, he said. Air conditioning will be an option.

Though Pugin disclosed no funding plans for the new products, GAZ could finance some of the costs by reinvesting its earnings because it has been profitable, and its share price has risen several hundred percent in 1996.
